cells.tense: You have gathered what matters and you are holding it, calmly, on purpose.
cells.ask: Offer the invitation to join what you're holding — one person, one open door, nothing required back.
cells.core:
You know what you're standing for, and you're still standing in it. Nothing has scattered you. You pulled your energy in from everywhere it had drifted and aimed it at the thing worth keeping — and it holds, without strain. When someone in your care is shortchanged, you feel it and you correct it, and you don't keep score while you do.

That steadiness is where people get to find each other. Because you're not white-knuckling it, there's room in the room. What you're protecting can be shared now instead of only guarded, and the sharing is the point. Ask one person in, with no conditions on what they bring back — that's the door this opens.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding direction steady, and there's room for others in it.
cells.verb: gathering what was scattered and holding the one direction worth defending

cells.tense: You're defending a fight that hasn't arrived yet, every conversation already a standoff.
cells.ask: Set the defense down for one hour and let your mind go quiet — let the next move come from being clear instead of being braced.
cells.core:
When this runs well, you protect what's yours because you can see exactly where the line is, and you move when moving helps. You rally the people who share the load and you hold the point together, and the fairness of it is obvious to everyone in the room.

But you're holding the line so hard you've started holding lines nobody's crossing. Every conversation runs a trial; every choice gets checked against a balance that hasn't tipped yet. The defense got big enough to become the whole relationship. What's missing isn't courage — it's a mind that can rest long enough to see straight. The direction you're protecting came from somewhere real, and it doesn't need fear to survive. Let yourself stop computing for one hour. Sit with the complication without solving it, and what you decide from there you can actually keep.
cells.sheetLine: You're braced against a fight that isn't here yet.

cells.tense: You stopped gathering a while back, and you're still standing where the push stopped.
cells.ask: Let one thing end that has already ended — say goodbye to it plainly and keep what it made.
cells.core:
When this is alive, you stand for the fair thing even when it costs you, and the people around you count on that. You gather what's needed, you say what you'll defend, and you stay at the post until the matter settles. It doesn't take drama — it takes you being there.

Something worth holding is still worth holding, and you're not holding it anymore. You pulled your weight off the line some time ago. The direction is still yours; the standing stopped. Everything that could have gathered around it has drifted. What's starved isn't the will — it's the ground under it. Something already finished hasn't been set down, and that unset weight is what your hands are full of instead. End it out loud, just once. Say it's over and mean it, and keep the piece of it that was real. The ground clears, and standing gets possible again.
cells.sheetLine: You have something worth holding and you've stopped holding it.

cells.tense: You're already holding the line — you just talk about it like it's holding itself.
cells.ask: Claim one quiet correction you made this week — say 'I'm keeping this' — and let the claim stand on its own.
cells.core:
The gift of this is plain: when it's working, you keep things level for people who can't do it themselves, and you never make them ask twice. The scales come back even around you, and nobody has to be told it was you.

You decide what holds and what doesn't, every day, in small adjustments nobody sees — and you describe it as circumstances working themselves out. The choosing is running constantly. You're just not claiming it. The spare handed to whoever came up short, the person everyone dropped who you stood beside — that didn't happen to you; you did that. Give one of those its name out loud.
cells.sheetLine: You're already choosing what to hold. The claim on it is still unclaimed.
